The questions I get.

Real answers · Pre-empted
Will the customer know it's a bot texting them?

The text says "Hi, on the tools — couldn't get to the phone." It reads exactly like you'd reply if you had 10 seconds between jobs. Most customers don't notice — they just want their job sorted. Once they reply, the AI captures their info naturally.

What if I'm somewhere with no signal?

Your CallCatch number is a separate, dedicated mobile number that lives in the cloud — not on your physical phone. As long as Twilio (the SMS network we use) is up, missed calls still get the text-back. Your phone signal only matters for receiving the final lead summary, and that lands the moment you're back in coverage.

Can I cancel anytime?

Yes. No contract, no notice period. During the free trial there's no card on file — I literally can't charge you. After the trial, you stay on £45/mo until you tell me to stop. WhatsApp me "cancel" and I deactivate your number same day.

What if the AI says something stupid to my customer?

Honest answer: the AI is very good at extracting name/postcode/job from a message, but it's not perfect. If a customer sends something genuinely confusing, the AI will still pass you the raw text so you have full context. You're never relying on the AI alone — you always see the original message too.

How is this different from voicemail?

Voicemail is one-way and slow — customers rarely leave one, and when they do you can't reply by text. CallCatch starts a real text conversation in seconds, captures structured info (name, postcode, problem, urgency), and delivers it ready-to-call. Higher response rate, faster turnaround.

What happens after the 21-day trial?

Day 18 I'll WhatsApp you and ask: "Worth continuing or not?" If yes — £45/mo, paid by bank transfer or Stripe (your choice). If no — I deactivate your number and we part ways. No automatic charges, no surprise emails.
